pr.title: Run Check on the release pull request the Release workflow opens
pr.head: 6c3bfb9d85ecd787a6deb5927ac834aa194c0850

summary: Projector ships a release through its Release workflow, .github/workflows/release.yml. You start it by hand, and its propose job bumps the version on a release/vX.Y.Z branch and opens a pull request for it. Merging that pull request tags and publishes the release. The Check workflow, .github/workflows/check.yml, runs the TypeScript checks, the Python tests, and project check on every pull request.

Until this change, a release pull request never got those checks. The propose job pushes the branch and opens the pull request with the workflow's own token, GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub starts no workflow run for an event that token causes. The exceptions are workflow_dispatch and repository_dispatch.

The change uses the first exception. Check gains a workflow_dispatch trigger, and the propose job, now granted actions: write, runs gh workflow run check.yml --ref "$branch" as its last command. The dispatched run checks out the release branch, so its check job reports on the branch's head commit, which is the pull request's head. The docs explain the dispatch and why it exists.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One full review at 6c3bfb9, clean, with no finding threads.
  • One suggestion: the docs and comments call workflow_dispatch the only event the workflow token can trigger, but repository_dispatch is the other, and the publish job uses it.
  • The dispatch cannot run until this merges, because GitHub dispatches a workflow only when its default-branch file has the trigger. The next release is the first real test.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Workflow token: GITHUB_TOKEN, the token GitHub gives each workflow run. Events it causes start no new run, except a dispatch.
  • Dispatch: a request, such as gh workflow run, that starts a workflow on a named branch.
  • propose job: the Release workflow job that bumps the version and opens the release pull request.

groups.title: The Release workflow dispatches Check on its branch
groups.kicker: A new trigger on Check and a dispatch at the end of the propose job
intro: The workflow token cannot start Check through a push or a pull request, but it can dispatch it. The propose job now does that after it opens the release pull request, or after it finds one already open on a rerun. The dispatch names the release branch, so GitHub runs the branch's copy of check.yml, which has the new trigger because the branch is cut from main.
The dispatched Check run keeps the workflow's contents: read permission and runs code the Release workflow itself committed from main, so it reaches no secrets and runs no outside code.

checks.text: No branch protection or ruleset on main requires a status check, so the dispatched job's name, check, cannot mismatch a required check. The review read both from the GitHub API.

files.note: Adds workflow_dispatch as a trigger, with a comment that says the Release workflow uses it.

checks.text: The comment says workflow_dispatch is "the exception" GitHub allows for the workflow token. repository_dispatch is the other exception, and the publish job in release.yml relies on it. Consider naming both. The review lists this as a suggestion, not a finding.

files.note: Grants the propose job actions: write, dispatches Check on the release branch as the step's last command, and updates the Testing text the job writes into the release pull request.

checks.text: A job-level permissions block replaces the workflow-level one, so the job lists contents: write and pull-requests: write again beside the new scope. gh workflow run needs actions: write.

The dispatch runs after both branches of the gh pr list check, so a rerun that finds the pull request already open also dispatches Check on the new force-pushed head. A failed dispatch fails the step under set -euo pipefail, and a rerun repeats it. The review extracted the step's script and ran bash -n on it.

groups.title: The release docs explain the dispatch
groups.kicker: docs/plugins.md and docs/develop.md describe why Check is dispatched
intro: docs/plugins.md, under "Release an update", gains a paragraph on why the Release workflow dispatches Check and what that requires. docs/develop.md, under "Release", gains one sentence that says the same and links there.

files.note: A new paragraph explains the workflow-token rule, the dispatch, and the two configuration changes it needs.

checks.text: "workflow_dispatch is the one event that token may trigger" is not accurate: repository_dispatch also starts a run, and the publish job's site rebuild uses it. docs/projects/proposed-projects/readme.md names both. The review lists this as a suggestion, not a finding.

files.note: One sentence in "Release" says the workflow dispatches Check on the release pull request, and why.
